---
title: "Home runs"
---

```{r}
#| message: false
#| cache: true
library(tidyverse)
library(Lahman)

shortened_seasons <- c(1918, 1919, 1981, 1994, 1995, 2020)

hr_by_season <- Teams |>
  group_by(yearID) |>
  summarise(
    total_home_runs = sum(HR, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_team_games = sum(G, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(season = yearID) |>
  mutate(
    home_runs_per_game = total_home_runs / total_team_games,
    shortened = season %in% shortened_seasons
  )
```

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)

hr_by_season |>
  ggplot(aes(x = season, y = home_runs_per_game)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(
    data = filter(hr_by_season, shortened),
    aes(color = "Shortened season"),
    size = 2.5
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Shortened season" = "firebrick")) +
  labs(
    title = "Home runs per game by season",
    x = "Season",
    y = "Home runs per game",
    color = "Season type",
    caption = "Source: Lahman Baseball Database"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The seasonal drop in 1981, 1994, and 2020 is tied to shortened or disrupted schedules, which reduced total team-games and therefore lowered the total home run count.

```{r}
#| message: false
comparison <- hr_by_season |>
  filter(season %in% c(2019, 1981, 1994, 2020)) |>
  arrange(match(season, c(2019, 1981, 1994, 2020))) |>
  select(
    Season = season,
    `Total home runs` = total_home_runs,
    `Total team-games` = total_team_games,
    `Home runs per game` = home_runs_per_game
  )

knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 3)
```

This page explores home run trends in Major League Baseball.
